models.collectorNote: French-market survivors dominate; the Facel-bodied coupés are the blue-chip Arondes and priced accordingly.

generations.name: Aronde (9 Aronde / Flash)
generations.note: The Flash engine replaced the Fiat-derived unit in 1956; sporting Grand Large and Plein Ciel/Océane coupés were bodied by Facel.

generations.name: Aronde P60
generations.note: The squared-off P60 restyle modernised the range; the Montlhéry and Étoile versions spanned taxi to near-sporting.

models.intro: The swallow (hirondelle, hence the badge) that made Simca France's second carmaker: a modern monocoque saloon with the Flash engine, sold in everything from taxi trim to the elegant Facel-built coupés. Over 1.4 million were made.

models.collectorNote: Flathead parts knowledge lives in the early-Ford world; French V8 survivors are few, Brazilian cars (with the later Hemi 'Emi-Sul') are a parallel universe.

generations.name: Vedette / Chambord / Présidence
generations.note: The Aquillon engine was Ford's French V8-60 development; the Présidence was the flag-trim flagship.

models.intro: Ford of France's V8, inherited whole when Simca bought the Poissy plant in 1954: a flathead 2.4-litre V8 in an American-styled saloon, Versailles, Trianon, Régence, then the Présidence and the Chambord. France's last V8-engined production car of its era, and the seed of Brazil's Simca do Brasil.

models.collectorNote: Rallye 2/3 provenance is documented by the club registries, replicas exist. Rear-engined handling rewards respect and good dampers.

generations.name: 1000 / Rallye 1–3
generations.note: Road cars ran 39–60 hp across the range; the Rallye 3's 1,294 cc engine made 103 hp and wore its arches and stripes from the factory.

models.intro: Simca's rear-engined answer to the Renault 4 and the Beetle era: a square-cut four-door with the Poissy engine behind the rear axle, built for seventeen years and rallied hard in its Rallye forms, the Rallye 2 and 3 are homologation-bred tarmac weapons with a cult following.

models.collectorNote: Survival in France is better than export markets; the Ti is the collector car, the Rancho the cult one. Check the hatch aperture and sills for rust.

generations.name: 1100 / Ti
generations.note: The Ti's twin-carburettor 1,294 cc engine made 82–83 hp and gave the hatchback genuine pace; the Rancho added the outdoor costume on the same bones.

models.intro: One of the first true hatchbacks: transverse engine, front-wheel drive, a folding rear seat and a hatch, years before the Golf defined the class. The 1100 Ti and the Matra-Simca Rancho (the leisure off-roader it sired) show the range's reach; nearly 2.9 million were built.
